source_review.notes: Checked six official/primary sources. Reactive Streams supports receiver demand preceding delivery, nonblocking asynchronous backpressure, bounded subscriber-controlled queues, and publisher delivery not exceeding requested elements. RFC 9113 supports directional hop-local stream/connection byte windows, DATA-only flow control, receiver authority, and prompt control-frame reading. gRPC supports streaming flow control, local buffering caveats, cancellation, and duplex deadlock warning. RabbitMQ supports acknowledgement/prefetch window semantics and consumer-overload cautions. Kafka design supports consumer pull.

evidence: Checked cumulative demand D, delivery N, revoked unused credit X, outstanding O, window W, buffer B_j/K_j, producer lambda, consumer mu, feedback R, prefetch P, service S, concurrency I, and fan-out F for consistent units and scopes.
Confirmed cumulative quantities and instantaneous occupancy are not conflated.
Confirmed the lambda<mu stability statement is qualified by effective admission and a terminal policy when the source cannot slow.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Credit equations bind the credited unit only, not decoded size or downstream cost.

evidence: Recomputed 200 messages/s times 0.1 s as 20 pipeline-fill items and 400/s times 0.05 s as 20.
Recomputed 50 upstream items times fan-out 20 as 1,000 downstream calls.
Recomputed unslowable-source backlog growth as 1,000-100=900 events/s.

Recomputed ten consumers times 1,000 prefetch as 10,000 and one hundred as 100,000; summed buffers 100+200+50+150=500 and added 50 in-service plus 30 transport for 580; counted ten examples and five answer pairs.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Prefetch/window figures are starting scenarios requiring measured latency, variability, cost, and protocol-race evidence.

evidence: Derived N<=D and 0<=O<=W from demand-before-delivery, atomic spend, bounded grant, and unused-credit revocation.
Derived total explicit buffer bound as the sum of hop bounds plus separately bounded in-service/transport work.
Constructed fan-out counterexample proving upstream concurrency does not bound downstream calls.
Derived linear backlog growth lambda-mu when source rate permanently exceeds consumer service and cannot respond to pressure.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Each argument names the hidden queue, unit-expansion, bypass, or rate assumption that can invalidate it.

evidence: Reviewed zero/one/unlimited/overflow credit, small/large windows, delayed/duplicate controls, cancellation, expiry, generation change, reconnect, and restart.
Reviewed encoded-to-decoded expansion, heterogeneous cost, batching, fan-out, merge/join/broadcast, slow subscriber, impossible-to-slow sources, drops, coalescing, and durable spill.
Reviewed acknowledgement before/after receipt/durable handoff/effect, redelivery, lease expiry, partition pause, rebalance, ordering, idempotency, and retention-sized recovery.
Reviewed duplex zero-window deadlock, blocked control, lock cycles, hostile producers, forged priority, autoscaling window multiplication, unfair shared credit, and synchronized resume.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Coverage spans protocol, resource, semantic, temporal, topology, recovery, fairness, and hostile behavior.

evidence: Confirmed demand precedes delivery and credit unit/scope/lifetime are explicit.
Confirmed every named buffer has a count/byte/age bound and cancellation removes future interest.
Confirmed acknowledgement never implies a later milestone than the documented ownership transfer.
Confirmed fan-out branches acquire downstream capacity and retries cannot bypass it.
Confirmed control progress remains possible under data pressure and recovery grants credit gradually.
invariant_checking.notes: Transport flow control is never presented as an end-to-end application-capacity guarantee.

evidence: Reviewed credit proof and confirmed element credit alone cannot bound bytes or resource cost.
Reviewed pipeline sum and confirmed one hidden unbounded buffer invalidates it.
Reviewed fan-out example and confirmed downstream cap can increase upstream residence, requiring deadline/admission adjustment.
Reviewed rate mismatch and confirmed pressure cannot stabilize an exogenous source without terminal loss/storage/rejection policy.
proof_review.notes: Arguments are conditional resource bounds, not delivery/exactly-once guarantees.

evidence: Confirmed four arguments are labeled and separated from protocol-specific behavior.
Confirmed HTTP/2, gRPC, Reactive Streams, RabbitMQ, and Kafka semantics are attributed to their own scopes.
Confirmed sizing equations and policies are presented as estimates to test, not normative defaults.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Protocol conformance, design policy, and empirical capacity claims remain distinct.

evidence: All six official/primary references were checked on 2026-09-02 where current guidance applies.
All rates, latencies, windows, expansion ratios, fan-out, buffer sizes, and fleet counts are labeled scenarios.

Safe prefetch, bandwidth-delay needs, decoded cost, service variance, races, lease behavior, broker retention, fair allocation, autoscaling, and recovery remain explicit integration/load/fault evidence obligations.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No production transport, broker, consumer fleet, stream library, or workload was empirically assessed.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed credit protocol, units/expansion, hidden buffers, synchronous and streaming translation, acknowledgements/prefetch, leases/rebalance, fan-out/merge, unslowable sources, stability/deadlock, fairness, observability, and recovery verification as an end-to-end control model.

practitioner_review.notes: Checked implementability through a complete buffer inventory, explicit demand contracts, dual byte/count/cost gates, deadline-aware admission, ack milestone tables, downstream permits, control/read loops, lease-safe pause, bounded terminal policies, fleet-aware windows, and invariant tests.

pedagogical_review.notes: The module progresses from demand semantics through transport/application boundaries, brokers and call graphs, then instability, fairness, observability, and verification. Ten examples and five integrative exercises have complete answers.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
